findings.failureScenario: DesktopProvider polls getSnapshot every 1200 ms (250 ms while importing/exporting/jobs) and calls setSnapshot(next) unconditionally. The IPC result is always a fresh object, so the single memoized context value (snapshot, ui, dialog, error, ...) changes on every poll and every useDesktop() consumer re-renders even when nothing changed. During a long import/export the cadence is 4 Hz, and JobDialog adds its own 300 ms setInterval that also calls refresh(), so the whole shell re-renders and the host session owner serves a full snapshot several times a second while the user is trying to keep working.
findings.action: Skip setSnapshot when the new snapshot is structurally unchanged (compare a host-supplied revision/generation or a cheap hash), split rapidly changing status (jobs/progress) into its own context or selector so grid/inspector consumers do not subscribe to it, and drop JobDialog's separate interval in favour of the provider's single poll.

findings.failureScenario: Every non-UI command routed through run() (including read-only queries such as library.preferences, app.gpu, presets.list, photo.inspect and high-frequency edits) is followed by await refresh(), i.e. a full snapshot round trip through spawn_blocking and the session-owner channel before the caller's promise resolves. Opening Settings alone issues six queries, each chased by a snapshot; a burst of per-tick commands serialises on the snapshot latency instead of the command latency, working against the 16 ms slider budget.
findings.action: Refresh only after commands that mutate library/session state (or let the host return a revision in the command result and refresh only when it advanced), and do not await the refresh before resolving the command promise.

findings.failureScenario: ImportDialog keeps all review candidates (one per file in the chosen folder or card, unbounded) in component state and renders every one as a <label> with an ImportCandidatePreview in a plain map(). The same component owns the Keywords, Album, Destination, Rename and extension text fields, so each keystroke re-renders the entire candidate list, and each checkbox toggle copies the whole checked[] array and re-renders all rows. Importing a 5,000-photo card makes typing in any field and toggling selections visibly lag.
findings.action: Virtualize the candidate list (windowed rows with fixed height) and memoize the row component keyed by candidate and checked state; move form fields into a child component so typing does not re-render the list.

findings.failureScenario: gainmap::apply walks every pixel on one thread and, for each pixel, runs three bilinear gain.sample calls (four slice reads each) and three powf plus three exp2 even for the single-channel maps the encoder writes by default (channels==1 maps src=0 for all three channels, so the same sample and powf are computed three times). compute() likewise runs one log2 per pixel (three when multichannel) serially. On a 24 MP HDR gain-map export or decode this is on the order of seconds on one core while to_srgb8 and the JPEG encoder in the same pipeline use all cores, against the project's 1 s per 24 MP export budget.
findings.action: When gain.channels == 1 compute one sample and one powf per pixel and reuse it for the three channels; hoist the per-row y coordinate; and parallelise apply() and compute() by rows with lightcraft_raster::par_rows as the neighbouring code does.

findings.failureScenario: encode_png_pq and the planes build in encode_avif_hdr convert pixels in a single-threaded loop that calls pq_encode (two powf) three times per pixel, plus a luminance accumulation and a growing Vec; for a 24 MP HDR export that is roughly 144 M powf calls on one core before the encoder starts. encode_png additionally copies the whole U8 sample buffer with to_vec() (up to ~100 MB for 24 MP RGBA) before handing it to the png writer.
findings.action: Parallelise the per-pixel PQ/HLG conversion by rows (par_rows or rayon chunks, merging max/sum per chunk), use a lookup table for pq_encode, and pass the borrowed slice to write_image_data instead of copying it.

findings.failureScenario: Rule::matches re-derives rule-constant data for every photo: lower(value) allocates (even for numeric fields such as rating, via other.to_string().to_lowercase()), date rules re-parse the rule date with rule_date for every photo, and inLast/notInLast call now() (thread-local clone or civil() format), then shift_iso which re-parses the current time and two fixed bound dates and formats twice, and the text rule builds a 14-field joined string plus keywords.join and people().join per photo. Smart albums and filters call this per photo over the whole catalog (Catalog::album_contains and query filtering), so a 100k-photo library with an 'in the last' smart album pays several allocations and four date parses per photo on every re-evaluation.
findings.action: Compile a RuleSet once into a matcher (pre-lowered operand, parsed dates, a single now()/cutoff computed per evaluation pass) and evaluate that per photo; at minimum compute now()/shift_iso once per RuleSet::matches batch rather than once per photo.

findings.failureScenario: The comment at lines 450-451 records that a file dialog on the UI thread stopped the window answering the compositor, which then reported the app as hung (#191), and Services::picker moves its dialogs to a thread. The other services were not moved: pick_folder (used by Browse Folder, Move Folder To, Open Library, import dialogs), pick_files, pick_lightroom_catalog, pick_preset_files, save_preset_file and friends are called synchronously from the egui frame (left.rs:845 calls pick_folder inside the click handler), and open_url / reveal block on Command::status() for xdg-open (which can wait for a freshly launched browser or file manager) while the model-folder opener was already moved to a background task for that reason. Clicking Browse Folder freezes painting and input for as long as the dialog or launcher is open.
findings.action: Route the remaining pickers through the threaded PickRequest/picker path and run open_url/reveal on a background task (or spawn without waiting) like open_model_folder, delivering the result through the existing task callback.

findings.failureScenario: PrefsWriter::tick runs from eframe's logic() every frame and, every 3 s (or immediately when the library path changes), re-serialises the entire UiState with to_vec_pretty, compares it to the last write and, when anything changed, writes it on the UI thread with File::create, write_all, sync_all, rename and a directory sync_all. fsync on a busy disk, antivirus-scanned profile or network home regularly takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds, causing visible frame hitches whenever a panel is resized, a thumbnail slider is dragged or any persisted UI value changes.
findings.action: Do the serialisation snapshot on the UI thread but hand the bytes to a background writer thread (coalescing to the latest value), keeping sync_all there; keep the exit-time save synchronous.

findings.failureScenario: look extract accepts up to 256 sample files and decodes every one to a linear Rgb32f (12 bytes per pixel, up to 1024x1024 = about 12.6 MB each) into the decoded Vec before extract_linear is called on the whole slice, so peak memory is up to about 3.2 GB (about 2 GB for typical 3:2 samples) and every decode is serial. On a modest machine 256 rendered samples exhaust memory or swap even though the statistics only need an accumulator per sample.
findings.action: Stream: decode each sample, fold it into the look statistics (or a per-sample summary) and drop the buffer, decoding samples on a bounded worker pool; or lower the cap to what fits a fixed memory budget.
